outlook: Corn and soybeans rallied into Wednesday's close ahead of the Thanksgiving break, on fund buying and short covering, a weaker dollar and continued Chinese soybean purchases; traders also reacted to a USTR clarification that Section 301 tariffs on China are capped at 20%. December corn finished near $4.39¾ and January soybeans near $12.44, while Chicago wheat slipped about 4¼ cents to $5.65½ on December liquidation and slow exports. Minneapolis December spring wheat bucked that, gaining 4¾ cents to $6.41½, and ICE January canola eased C$1.90 to C$771.30 but finished well off its lows on solid demand. US markets are closed today and close early Friday, with December contracts rolling ahead of Monday's first notice day.
